def flatten(items: list, depth: int = -1) -> list:
    """
    Flatten a nested list up to `depth` levels deep.
    
    depth=-1: fully flatten (unlimited recursion)
    depth=0:  return shallow copy (no flattening)
    depth=k:  flatten up to k levels
    
    Only `list` instances are expanded; all other types are treated as atomic.
    """
    result = []
    for item in items:
        if isinstance(item, list) and depth != 0:
            # Recurse: if depth is -1, keep it -1; otherwise decrement
            next_depth = depth - 1 if depth > 0 else -1
            result.extend(flatten(item, next_depth))
        else:
            result.append(item)
    return result

When depth=k (k>0), decrement on each recursive call. I use isinstance(item, list) to ensure only lists are expanded, treating strings, tuples, dicts, sets, etc. as atomic values.
